title: Spiti on a budget: real costs for 2026
meta_description: Spiti on a budget: HRTC bus fares, homestay prices, shared taxi rates, daily costs and a sample 8-night plan for about ₹22,000–32,000 per person.
summary: A Spiti trip by HRTC bus, shared taxi and family homestay costs about ₹2,000–3,500 a person a day in 2026. An 8-night circuit comes to roughly ₹22,000–32,000, excluding travel to Shimla or Manali. Buses, homestays with meals and shared village loops are the three biggest savings.

sections.heading: What a budget day in Spiti really costs
paras: Spiti is not expensive by Himalayan standards, but it is remote, and almost everything that reaches Kaza comes up one of two long roads. That shows in the price of a cafe meal and in taxi rates. The good news is that the two largest costs for a budget traveller, transport and beds, have honest cheap options: HRTC buses on every main route and family homestays in nearly every village.

Our working figure is ₹2,000–3,500 a person a day on twin sharing. The lower end assumes buses, homestays with dinner and breakfast, and simple lunches. The upper end adds one shared taxi loop every two or three days, a hostel private room in Kaza and the odd cafe dinner. All prices here are indicative for 2026; fares and fees change, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Buses: the backbone of a cheap trip
paras: Himachal Road Transport Corporation buses reach Kaza from both sides. From Manali, a bus usually leaves very early in the morning in season, about mid-June to October, and takes 10–12 hours over Kunzum La. From the Kinnaur side, buses run from Reckong Peo to Kaza through Nako and Tabo, usually once a day, and that road is open for much more of the year. Inside Spiti, local buses connect Kaza with Kibber, Langza on some days, and Mudh in the Pin valley, usually leaving Kaza in the afternoon and returning next morning.

That timing pattern matters. Village buses are designed for villagers going home after a day in Kaza, so they are ideal for a night in a homestay and awkward for a day trip. Plan your nights around them and you can see most of Spiti for a few hundred rupees. Women travel at half fare on HRTC buses within Himachal Pradesh under the state scheme, which makes a bus circuit very cheap for women; check current status before you travel.
list: Board at the starting stand when you can; seats run out mid-route in July and August.
Ask your host the evening before for the bus time; timetables change by season.
Carry small notes for the conductor and a snack; dhaba stops are short.

sections.heading: Homestays and hostels
paras: Family homestays are the best value in the valley. For ₹1,200–2,500 a person you get a room, often with thick blankets and a bed or floor mattresses, plus a home-cooked dinner and breakfast. Bathrooms may be shared and hot water may come by bucket. Since a cafe meal in Kaza costs ₹300–600, booking meals with the room saves a lot over a week. Villages with good clusters of homestays include Nako, Tabo, Dhankar, Kibber, Langza and Mudh.

In Kaza, Zostel Spiti offers dorm beds and private rooms, and family homestays in Kaza Khas, the old village, are similar in price to those elsewhere. Tabo's monastery guest house is a simple, cheap option next to the old complex. Comfort hotels in Kaza start at about ₹3,500 a night for a double, so they are not far beyond a budget if two people share.

sections.heading: Shared taxis without overpaying
paras: Kaza's taxi union posts fixed rates for every route on a board near its office. Check the board before any conversation about price, and you will not be overcharged. A taxi seats four to six people, so the trick is to fill it. Hostels and cafes in Kaza are where travellers form groups for the next day's loop; ask the evening before.

The two most useful shared days are the northern loop to Key, Kibber and Chicham, and the plateau loop to Langza, Hikkim and Komic. Many people combine them in one long day; split four ways, that costs about ₹1,000–1,500 each. A drop at the Chandratal camps from Kaza costs ₹6,000–8,000 per car, so it too is far cheaper shared.

sections.heading: A sample 8-night budget plan
paras: This is the plan we give students and solo travellers who ask how to do Spiti for around ₹25,000. It enters from Kinnaur for a slow climb and leaves by Manali when Kunzum La is open. Totals assume twin sharing in homestays with two meals, buses on main legs and one shared taxi day, excluding travel to Reckong Peo and from Manali.
list: Night 1, Nako: bus from Reckong Peo, homestay by the lake.
Nights 2–3, Tabo: bus, monastery guest house or homestay, a rest day.
Nights 4–6, Kaza: bus, hostel or homestay, one shared taxi loop.
Night 7, Mudh: afternoon local bus, homestay, dawn ibex walk.
Night 8, Kaza: morning bus back, early night before the Manali bus.
Day 9: HRTC bus or shared taxi seat over Kunzum La to Manali.

sections.heading: Ten ways to spend less
paras: Most savings come from the same few habits: slow travel, shared vehicles and eating where you sleep. The rest come from avoiding the peak weeks.
list: Travel in the first half of June or in September, when room prices drop.
Take the bus over a shared taxi seat on the long legs.
Book homestays with dinner and breakfast included.
Fill a taxi with four people for every village loop.
Sleep in villages on bus nights instead of hiring cars for day trips.
Carry a steel bottle and refill filtered water at homestays and cafes.
Bring enough cash; a failed ATM can force an expensive detour.
Buy snacks and dry fruit in Reckong Peo or Manali before you arrive.
Avoid long weekends and the Ladarcha fair days if you want cheap rooms.
Skip the Chandratal camp and see the lake from a Manali-bound taxi stop if money is tight.

sections.heading: Where not to cut corners
paras: Do not save money by rushing. A cheap trip that goes from Manali to Kaza in one day and then straight up to Langza is the classic way to get altitude sickness, and a medical evacuation costs far more than two extra homestay nights. Keep a spare day for landslides in July and August. Buy travel insurance that covers high-altitude road travel, and talk to your doctor before you go. Finally, pay your homestay hosts fairly; their prices are already low for the work involved.

faqs.q: How much does a Spiti trip cost on a budget?
faqs.a: About ₹2,000–3,500 a person a day in 2026 with buses, shared taxis and homestays. An 8-night circuit is roughly ₹22,000–32,000, excluding travel to Shimla or Manali. Prices are indicative and change each season.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to reach Kaza?
faqs.a: The HRTC bus. From Manali it costs about ₹400–600 and runs in season, about mid-June to October. From Reckong Peo, buses run most of the year through Nako and Tabo. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a homestay cost in Spiti?
faqs.a: About ₹1,200–2,500 a person a night with dinner and breakfast. Village homestays in Kibber, Langza and Mudh are usually at the lower end; Kaza can be higher in July and August.
Possibly for 5–6 nights if you travel by bus, stay in dorms or the simplest homestays and share every taxi. It leaves little room for delays. We would not plan a full circuit on that amount.

faqs.q: Do women get a bus discount in Himachal?
faqs.a: Yes, women have been travelling at half fare on HRTC buses within Himachal Pradesh. Rules can change, so check current status before you travel.
Kaza has ATMs, but they can run out of cash in season and fail when the network is down. Carry enough cash for several days; village homestays prefer cash.

faqs.q: Is a shared taxi worth it over the bus?
faqs.a: On long legs, the bus is far cheaper. Shared taxis are worth it for village loops from Kaza, which buses do not cover in one day, and when the bus is full.
Early June and September, outside the peak school-holiday and long-weekend weeks. May and October are cheaper still but only via Kinnaur, and some places are closed.

faqs.q: Do I need to book homestays in advance?
faqs.a: In July, August and on long weekends, yes, at least a day ahead. At other times you can usually find a room on arrival, but phone ahead to be safe.
